mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY growth > 3% does not correlate with negative SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase > 0.5% MoM does not correlate with negative SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a supply shock, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decrease > 1% MoM does not correlate with negative SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% year-over-year, it signals a restrictive monetary policy in a slowing economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of FEDFUNDS > 4% and GDPC1 YoY < 2% does not correlate with negative SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a single month signals weakening labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or PAYEMS decrease > 100,000 MoM does not correlate with negative SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or RSAFS increase > 1% MoM does not correlate with positive SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it signals an accommodative monetary policy in a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: accommodative policy with strong labor market
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of FEDFUNDS < 1% and UNRATE < 4% does not correlate with positive SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).
